issues.display_title: Issue #778: A legacy project with no stored coordSpace re-normalises its map footprint on every geometry edit
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

video-778.mp4

Split out of #725 deliberately — the pivot fix landed without it, on the author's call, because this is a second mover with its own product consequence.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

computeCoordSpace (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:72) falls back to deriving the map anchor AND the metres-per-pixel scale from the live bounding box whenever canvasData.coordSpace is absent:

export function computeCoordSpace(canvasData: CanvasData | null): CoordSpace {
  if (canvasData?.coordSpace) return canvasData.coordSpace;
  ...
  // else: centre = live bbox centre, and the span is normalised to 50 m
  //       unless a level's floorplanMeta.scaleMmPerUnit puts it in 5–500 m

So on a project saved before coordSpace was persisted, any edit that changes the bounding box re-derives both the anchor and the scale. The building moves AND resizes on the map. #725 fixed the rotation pivot; this is the sibling that no pivot fix reaches, because it is the anchor and the scale, not the pivot.

Why it was split rather than folded into #725

Freezing it is a one-line change inside pinPlacement — coordSpace: cd.coordSpace ?? computeCoordSpace(cd), guarded on computeBBox(cd) !== null so an empty project is never pinned to the junk mpp = 50/500 fallback before its first floor exists.

The consequence is what needs a decision, not the code. Freezing at load means a legacy project's on-map size is fixed at whatever it was on that load. If that size came from a bad OCR scaleMmPerUnit, the user can no longer nudge it back by editing geometry and has to reach for the scale knob instead. Three independent reviewers raised this as a product call rather than an engineering one.

There is a second, narrower question inside it: computeCoordSpace prefers a level's scaleMmPerUnit when the resulting span lands between 5 m and 500 m. Freezing at load means a project whose first scan happens AFTER a reload keeps the frozen 50 m normalisation and silently loses that real-world scale — replaceLevelContent (src/lib/editor/levels.ts:85) and useAddLevel.ts:286 both read current.coordSpace ?? computeCoordSpace(next).

Suggested shape

  1. Decide whether freezing is right at all, or only for a project that already carries a non-identity placement. Gating on "a placement exists" keeps today's behaviour for unplaced projects and preserves the later-OCR path.
  2. If it is, fold it into pinPlacement with the empty-project guard, and add the case to src/lib/map/__tests__/placement-pivot.test.ts: a doc with no coordSpace, unrotated — after pinning, appending a level leaves an untouched point's lng/lat fixed. Plus the guard: pinning a geometry-less doc must NOT stamp a coordSpace, so the first floor drawn still normalises.
  3. src/hooks/useDigitalTwinExport.ts already recomputes coordSpace from freshly scanned levels; it drops the pivots alongside (#725), and should follow whatever rule this issue settles.

Related

  • #725 — the pivot half, merged. unpinPlacement exists precisely because a pivot and its coordSpace anchor have to move together; src/lib/map/__tests__/coordspace-proportional.test.ts locks that pairing and is where a fix here would be proven.

issues.display_title: Issue #780: Information and Event images 401 for anonymous visitors on /v/{key} — read them through the public share-key endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-780.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Every image on the public /v/{key} viewer that was uploaded through the editor is a 401 for anyone not signed in. Found while reviewing #776 (#250); the trace is alfarez21's, verified against the code on 21 Aug 2026.

What breaks

uploadProjectImage (src/lib/editor/uploadImage.ts:19) and the Event upload (src/components/editor/EventModal.tsx:61) both store a fully-formed URL string:

/api/files?projectId={id}&name={uuid}.jpg

hydratePersistedState writes informationRecords, categories, and eventRecords back verbatim (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:243-247) — unlike floorConfigs and uploadedFiles, they never pass through fileUrl(). So the stored ?projectId= form survives into the public viewer, and that branch of /api/files attaches a Bearer token from the session. A crawler or a logged-out visitor has none, and the Go endpoint (/v1/projects/:id/file, behind middleware.Auth()) answers 401.

Surfaces affected on /v/{key} and /embed/{key}: Information hero photos, Information logos, related-event thumbnails, EventPanel photos, PhotoPreviewModal, and the logo/photo chips on MapObjectMarkers.

Not affected: floor plan backdrops — the live viewer never requests them (floorConfigs[].fileUrl has one consumer, FloorplanEditor.tsx:519, editor-only; the viewer draws vector geometry from canvasData). Panorama thumbnails are external tourmkr URLs.

No backend work needed

GET /v1/live/:key/file?name= (API-GO#159, deployed) already serves any file of a published project anonymously, addressed by name. The names these records need are sitting in the stored URLs — they are the generated UUID names the backend assigned at upload. So the fix is entirely frontend.

Scope

  1. Generalize the share-card proxy. #776 adds src/app/api/live/[key]/image/route.ts, hard-wired to one object. Widen it (or add a sibling) to /api/live/[key]/file?name=, forwarding to /v1/live/{key}/file?name= with no credentials attached. Published-only and 404-identical are enforced upstream.
  2. Rewrite the stored URLs on hydrate for the public viewer. When hydrating from a share key, map any /api/files?projectId=…&name=X in informationRecords, categories, and eventRecords to /api/live/{key}/file?name=X. The editor and /preview keep the authenticated form — they have a session and their projects may still be drafts.
  3. Leave the persisted blob alone; this is a read-time rewrite. Records saved by older projects have to keep working without a migration.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening /v/{key} in a private window shows Information photos, logos, and Event photos — no 401s in the network panel
  • /embed/{key} behaves the same
  • The editor and /preview/{projectId} still load the same images through the authenticated path, including for draft projects
  • A project whose images predate this change needs no re-upload
  • Unit test covering the hydrate-time rewrite, including a record whose URL is already public or external (must be left untouched)

Depends on

  • API-GO#159 — deployed.
  • #776 — introduces the proxy route this widens; land that first to avoid a conflict.

issues.display_title: Issue #791: feat(routing): route step model, distance and time, and a real scaled-project predicate (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Source PRD: #770 · Design: #774 (Done on Project #106) · PRD doc: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-route-panel-redesign/prd.md on product-docs

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The pure-logic half of the route redesign, split out so the UI task has something correct to render. No component changes here.

Also fixes a live bug: a same-floor route returns status: "found" with transfers: [] (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:205-210), and the step list is gated on routeTransfers.length > 0 (src/components/editor/preview/DirectionPanel.tsx:160) — so a visitor whose trip stays on one floor sees "Route found" and no instructions at all. R22/R23.

Scope

src/lib/routing/routeSteps.ts (new, pure)

  • Build an ordered Step[] from segments + transfers. Types: walk | lift | stairs | outdoor | arrive.
  • It needs more than segments+transfers. R26 (floor left → floor reached) needs level names, and R50 (30 s per floor of stairs) needs floor order. LevelData has no elevation, floorNumber or order field (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:317-345; grep elevation across src/store → 0 hits), and FloorConfig only carries name/height (:24-32). Floor order is the array index inside the building group (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:785-803). So the module takes canvasData (or a pre-derived ordered level list), not just the route.
  • Every found route emits a leading Walk and a trailing Arrive. This is the single-floor fix.
  • Emit the intermediate walk steps between transfers too. Today only the first and last walk lines exist (DirectionPanel.tsx:162, :170), so a cross-building trip (lift → outdoor → lift) silently drops the connector names for everything after the first. R29.
  • Labels through accessTypeLabel / accessTypeColor (src/lib/floorplanEditor/accessTypes.ts), not raw transfer.kind (DirectionPanel.tsx:167 prints the raw key today).

src/lib/routing/routeDistance.ts (new, pure)

  • The three constants defined once: walking pace 1.2 m/s, lift 60 s, stairs 30 s per floor. Not per project, not configurable (R19, R50, R53).
  • Time rounds up to whole minutes; a sub-minute total renders the "under a minute" string, never 0 (R20).
  • Unscaled project → null for every distance and time value. No placeholder, no plan units, no pixels, no warning (R17, R18, R51).

isScaledProject() predicate

No such helper exists (grep -rni "isScaled|hasScale|isCalibrat|scaleKnown" src → 0 hits).

Corrections to the To-Do in #770 — verified against the code

  1. ?? connector-name bug — SPLIT OUT to #799, fixed there. multiLevelRoute.ts:273 passed "" straight through because ?? only catches null/undefined, so an Access marker whose name was cleared rendered a blank step. Fixed at the producer with a trim-guard, matching exit.door.name?.trim() || "Door" (:419). connectorName is now guaranteed non-empty, so routeSteps can rely on it. What remains here is R30's other half: route every step label through accessTypeLabel / accessTypeColor instead of the hardcoded "Lift" / "Stairs" strings that fix deliberately left in place (accessTypeLabel("stairs") returns "Stair", singular — a visitor-copy decision this task owns).

  2. The legacy entrance item is impossible as written. #770 asks the step model to "handle the legacy entrance connector type". RouteTransfer.kind is typed VerticalAccessType | "outdoor" (multiLevelRoute.ts:38) and VerticalAccessType = Exclude<AccessTypeKey, "entrance"> (accessTypes.ts:33). Legacy entrance markers are consumed as building doors (multiLevelRoute.ts:187-193) and emitted as kind: "outdoor", connectorName: name?.trim() || "Door" (:419-421). "entrance" can never reach routeSteps. Keep it only as a regression test asserting the legacy path resolves to an outdoor/Door step.

  3. The distance formula in #770 double-applies the scale. #770 says "distance = summed segment path length × mpp". RouteSegment.path is already lng/lat — toLngLatPath (multiLevelRoute.ts:124-131) has already applied both mpp and the per-level makeLevelPixelTransform rotation/scale (geojson-utils.ts:552-564). Multiplying again is wrong. The right primitive already exists and is unexported: geoLength(segments, lat) (multiLevelRoute.ts:139-147), cos-lat-corrected, already used at :403 as the door-picking ruler. Export it and convert degrees → metres once.

  4. The scale trap in #770 is real but understated — a !!scaleMmPerUnit predicate is wrong.

    • computeCoordSpace() (geojson-utils.ts:73-105) is non-nullable and has four exits, not one fallback: a stored canvasData.coordSpace short-circuit (:74, which may itself be a frozen copy of a fallback), a real scale (:90-94), the normalized 50 m span (:98-102, TARGET_METERS = 50 at :30), and a degenerate 50/500 = 0.1 (:105). An mpp is never evidence of real scale.
    • The 5–500 window is geojson-utils.ts:86-96 (if (spanMeters >= 5 && spanMeters <= 500) at :89), and it gates spanMeters — pxSpan * mpp, the union bbox of every level — not mpp. :83-85 takes the first level with a truthy scaleMmPerUnit and applies it project-wide.
    • Mappedin imports set scaleMmPerUnit: null (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:573) but a genuine metric coordSpace — mpp: 1 / PIXELS_PER_METER (:610). Those projects ARE scaled. A naive !!scaleMmPerUnit predicate hides distance on every imported project.

Tests

  • routeSteps: single-floor (two steps, never empty), multi-floor, cross-building with intermediate walk steps, unnamed connector (incl. empty string), legacy entrance → outdoor/Door.
  • routeDistance: scaled and unscaled paths, the Mappedin scaleMmPerUnit: null + metric coordSpace case, the sub-minute rounding boundary, stairs floor-span from level index.
  • No routing-engine behaviour change beyond the ?? → trim-guard fix (R49) — pin it with an existing-route test.

Consumed by: #792 (route result UI) → #793 (step selection) → #794 (compact layout).

Out of scope

Any component change. The panel keeps rendering the old block until the UI task lands.

Notes

  • Design deliverable #774 is screenshots only. The design/direction-route branch points at 3dc3705, which is behind development and carries zero commits of its own — there is no design code to integrate.
  • #779 (Multi Place Direction) names this PRD as prerequisite D0.
  • pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-route-step-model, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #802 -> development. Branch feature/791-route-step-model, commit c65ad65 (6 files, +627/-24).

src/lib/routing/routeSteps.ts — buildRouteSteps(route, { destination }). It turned out not to need canvasData after all: floor names are resolved in the view from the existing levelName prop, and floor order is only needed for the stairs time allowance, so it lives in routeDistance instead. The module is pure over MultiLevelRoute plus a destination label.

src/lib/routing/routeDistance.ts — WALKING_PACE_MPS / LIFT_TRANSFER_SECONDS / STAIRS_SECONDS_PER_FLOOR defined once, plus isScaledProject(), routeMetrics() (null for an unscaled project — no placeholder anywhere) and routeMinutes() (null below a minute, so the view says it in words).

src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts — realScaleMpp() split out of computeCoordSpace so model placement and the visitor-facing distance question share one 5-500 m window. METERS_PER_DEGREE_LAT exported instead of 111320 inline twice in pixelToLngLat. geoLength exported from multiLevelRoute.ts.

Tests — +21 across two new files. The two that carry the weight:

  • An integration case through the real planner (lift + cross-building) asserting ["walk","lift","walk","outdoor","walk","arrive"] with walk segmentIndex [0,1,3] and the outdoor step on 2. This pins the segments = transfers + 2 alignment against the producer rather than a fixture, and covers the legacy entrance marker resolving to a named outdoor step.
  • A distance band on a 3.5 m walk, sized to catch both scale traps: a double-applied mpp lands near 0.18, a missing degree-to-metre conversion near 3e-5.

Split out: #801 — a Mappedin import is metric (20 px/m) but writes scaleMmPerUnit: null, so it reports as unscaled. Importer change, and writing a real scale re-activates the 5-500 m window, which could move the model on the map for a site over 500 m across. Needs its own verification.

issues.display_title: Issue #792: feat(preview): rewrite the route result as status, summary and step timeline (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-792-route-result.mp4

Source PRD: #770 · Design: #774 (Done on Project #106) · Depends on #791 (route step model + distance)

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Rewrite the route result inside the Direction panel as three blocks — Status → Summary → Steps — consuming the routeSteps / routeDistance modules from the model task. One component serves all four surfaces (editor preview, /preview/[projectId], /v/[key], /embed/[key]), so everything here ships to all of them at once.

The whole route result is src/components/editor/preview/DirectionPanel.tsx:148-172 today: a status chip (:149-156) and a flat flex-col gap-1 of bare <span>s (:160-172).

Scope

Data plumbing (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx)

  • Call site is PreviewOverlay.tsx:916 (element 916-930, wrapper 913-932). #770 says :809 — that line is an unrelated reportObjectSelected handler inside MapObjectMarkers.
  • Pass routeResult.segments. It is already in scope (routeResult at :219) and already consumed three times in the same body — :250 origin-level switch, :259 activeRoutePath, :471 routeLines. This is a one-word prop add, not plumbing work.
  • Drop routeInstructionNames.fromName. It is a dead no-op: passed as routeResult.transfers[0]?.connectorName (:926) and consumed as routeInstructionNames?.fromName ?? routeTransfers[0].connectorName (DirectionPanel.tsx:162) — the two sides are the identical expression, so the ?? fallback can never fire. It is also the first connector, not the origin, so it cannot serve R9/R10. Replace it with a real origin-label prop derived from dirState.fromArea / dirState.fromPin.
  • Keep levelName (PreviewOverlay.tsx:171 → floorConfigs[].name, passed :923) and missingEntrances (:924) — both already correct.

Status — restyle only, do not rewrite

R4-R7 already work. statusText is an exhaustive Record<RouteStatus, string | null> covering all 7 values (DirectionPanel.tsx:32-40, type-checked against the union at multiLevelRoute.ts:20-27), and the missing-door override is already there (:58-60, No door in ${missingEntrances.join(" or ")}; producer multiLevelRoute.ts:358-366, only ever emitted with status: "no-entrance", so it cannot shadow another status). R3 is also already correct — PreviewOverlay.tsx:220 and :227 return idle, statusText.idle is null, so no empty frame is drawn before both endpoints are chosen.

What is missing is the visual treatment: the failure branch is a hardcoded #fef2f2 / #991b1b inline style (:152) that ignores dark mode. Move it onto tokens, and design the collapsed failure height so it does not look broken.

Summary — entirely new (R8-R14)

Origin and destination names, total distance, estimated time, floor changes, buildings, step count. Zero counts omitted, never rendered as "0". "Your pin" for a dropped-pin origin. Time presented as an estimate, not a promise. Distance/time absent entirely on unscaled projects, with no note and no placeholder.

Floor changes = transfers.filter(kind !== "outdoor").length; buildings = outdoor transfers + 1. Both derive from props already passed.

Steps — entirely new (R21-R31)

Vertical timeline with a visible connector between rows. Icon + text per step (icon alone is a named risk in PRD §9 — lift #aebfd6 and stairs #cdb9a0 are close). Floor badge showing floor left → floor reached: transfer.fromLevelId exists on the transfer and is unused today (:167 prints only levelName(transfer.toLevelId)). Building name on the outdoor step (already correct at :166). Per-step distance on walking steps only, no threshold. Truncation for long floor and building names.

Tokens

Stay on --editor-* (defined in src/app/globals.css, :root at :135, redefined in the dark block) so dark mode keeps working. Every colour and spacing value from the design, no raw hexes.

Copy

Success status, all five failure statuses, the building-missing-door status, the five step types, the pin-origin label, the sub-minute time label. Plain visitor language — no product jargon, no internal identifiers, no plan units or pixel values ever shown to a visitor.

Accessibility

Contrast for status colours, floor badges and the selected-step state in both themes. Screen-reader reading order follows travel order.

Tests

Component render tests following src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/DirectionAreaAutocomplete.test.tsx. Pin: a single-floor route renders two steps; an unscaled project renders no distance anywhere; a failure status renders no summary and no steps.

Out of scope

Step selection and the compact layout — separate tasks.

Notes

Design #774 is screenshots only; branch design/direction-route points at 3dc3705, behind development, zero commits of its own. Nothing to merge.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-route-result-ui, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #806 -> development. Branch feature/792-route-result-ui, commits a654159 and 36b705f.

New: src/components/editor/preview/RouteResult.tsx — StatusLine, Summary, StepRow as subcomponents in one file, so #793 has a seam for selection state and #794 has one for the compact variant.

Design (#774) settled what the PRD left open. A found status is a small uppercase accent pill, not a banner — it must not compete with the summary. A failure is a full-width tinted box with no summary and no steps under it. Transfer copy is Take {connectorName} to {floor} (the design reads "Take Escalator 3 to Level 2"), so it uses the connector's own name rather than its type. The first walk says Walk from {origin} to {target}; later walks only say where they are heading. Arrival carries the accent solidly, since it is a destination rather than an instruction. The dropped-pin field was restyled to match ("Pin set — tap the map to move it").

Dark mode: the old status colours were inline hexes with no dark counterpart. --red-accent / --red-accent-dim added beside --blue-accent-dim, same alpha-on-oklch idiom, re-stated in .dark because --destructive lifts there.

Props: route replaces routeStatus + routeTransfers + missingEntrances. routeInstructionNames deleted — fromName was a no-op (identical expression on both sides of its own ??) and carried a connector name rather than an origin.

Bug the demo caught, tests did not (36b705f): the endpoint resolver returned option.area.name, but an Information-linked area usually has no name of its own — the visible label is the Information title. The empty string then survived a ?? guard, and every route printed Arrive at with nothing after it. Both sides trim-guarded. The old toName had the same flaw, so the destination has been unnamed in the step list for as long as the list has existed.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/792/video-792-route-result.mp4, 1920x1080 / 60 fps / 124 s. Four scenes, each asserting its own copy: the single-floor route that used to render nothing, a cross-building trip with its counts and outdoor step, a dropped-pin origin reading "Your pin", and a failure collapsing to its reason alone. Not in the video: the lift/stairs step and its floor badge — the shared demo project has no vertical connector at all, so a cross-floor trip inside it fails with "No access point on this floor" (that is scene 4). Covered by unit tests instead.

issues.display_title: Issue #799: fix(routing): an Access marker with a cleared name renders a blank route step (#770)
issues.main_description_html:
Found while validating PRD #770 against the code. Standalone bug, independent of the redesign — it is visible in the Direction panel today.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Bug

src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:273

connectorName: originConnector.name ?? (originConnector.type === "lift" ? "Lift" : "Stairs"),

?? only substitutes for null / undefined. AccessPoint.name is name?: string (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:160), so an Access marker whose name field was cleared in the editor carries "" — a real value that ?? passes straight through.

The route step then renders Walk to with nothing after it (src/components/editor/preview/DirectionPanel.tsx:162), on every surface Direction runs on: editor preview, /preview/[projectId], /v/[key] and /embed/[key].

Why this line and not the others

The rest of the codebase already guards with a trim, three times over — this line is the only outlier:

Location Guard
multiLevelRoute.ts:419 (cross-building door) exit.door.name?.trim() || "Door"
panel/AccessList.tsx:35 p.name?.trim() || \Access ${i + 1}``
PreviewOverlay.tsx:654 ap.name || accessTypeLabel(ap.type)

So "" is already an assumed-reachable value everywhere else that reads an Access name.

Fix

Trim-guard at the producer, matching :419:

connectorName: originConnector.name?.trim() || (originConnector.type === "lift" ? "Lift" : "Stairs"),

One line, in the one place every caller routes through — not a fallback bolted onto the view.

Deliberately unchanged

The hardcoded "Lift" / "Stairs" ternary stays as-is here. Swapping it for accessTypeLabel() would also change the visitor-facing string to "Stair" (singular — accessTypes.ts:11), which is a copy decision that belongs to the route-result rewrite. #791 already owns routing every step label through accessTypeLabel / accessTypeColor; this task is only the blank-label bug.

Scope

  • src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:273 — ?? → trim-guard.
  • Regression test in src/lib/routing/__tests__/multiLevelRoute.test.ts (existing canvas() fixture): a spanning connector named "" still produces a non-empty connectorName.

No routing-engine behaviour change — the path, the status and the chosen connector are all identical; only the label differs. Satisfies R49 of PRD #770.

Relates to

  • Source PRD: #770
  • #791 route step model — inherits this producer and assumes connectorName is non-empty.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green. Branch feature/<issue#>-connector-name-blank, PR targets development.

RESULT

PR #800 → development. Branch feature/799-connector-name-blank, commit 7d2e436 (2 files, +24/-1).

multiLevelRoute.ts:276 now reads originConnector.name?.trim() || (originConnector.type === "lift" ? "Lift" : "Stairs"), with a comment naming why ?? was wrong. The hardcoded type strings were left in place on purpose — see the "Deliberately unchanged" note above; #791 owns that copy decision.

Regression test added to src/lib/routing/__tests__/multiLevelRoute.test.ts on the existing canvas() fixture, with the connector name set to " " so the trim is exercised rather than a bare empty-string check. Verified it fails without the fix: AssertionError: expected ' ' to be 'Lift'.

issues.display_title: Issue #795: Add Floor import drops all Information and Category records, leaving every polygon link dangling
issues.main_description_html:
Split out of #733 (checkbox 1: "Polygon shapes imported from the file do not automatically link to information").

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

Importing a Mappedin ZIP through the editor's Add Floor produces polygons whose Information links all dangle: the geometry carries infoId, but the records those ids point at are never put in the store. Every linked polygon then disappears from the viewer, because PreviewOverlay filters on informationRecords.some(r => r.id === a.infoId).

Measured on the issue's own asset (mall-demo-consumer.zip, 34 locations / 36 geometryAnchors), running the real pipeline over both commit paths:

WIZARD  commit: {"linked":34,"dangling":0}   records staged: 34
EDITOR  Add-Level commit: {"linked":0,"dangling":34}   records staged: 0

Root cause

handleConfirmImport (src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:193-220) calls mergeImportIntoProject and then writes setCanvasData / setFloorConfigs / keepImportedFloorSettings / selectBuilding / setActiveLevelId — but never reads importSource.informationRecords or .categories. A grep for either name across the whole src/components/editor/add-level/ directory returns zero hits.

The wizard path does it right, two lines, on the same MappedinSource object:

// src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:180-182
if (src.informationRecords.length > 0 || src.categories.length > 0) {
  useMapStore.setState({ informationRecords: src.informationRecords, categories: src.categories });
}

So the converter is not at fault. convertLocations produces all 34 records and buildAnchorMap (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:211-220) writes infoId onto 34 of the 36 anchors — the exact field the manual "Link Information" UI writes and reads. An imported link is indistinguishable from a hand-made one.

Suggested shape

  1. Stage the records in handleConfirmImport alongside the levels. Not a straight copy like the wizard's — Add Floor merges into an existing project, so it must append and de-duplicate by id against the store's current informationRecords/categories, or a second import of the same venue doubles every record.
  2. Consider moving the staging into mergeImportIntoProject (src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts) so both entry points share one implementation and the wizard's replace-vs-append difference becomes explicit rather than accidental.
  3. Test: import the sample twice through Add Floor — 34 records after the first, still 34 after the second, and dangling === 0 both times.

Not in scope

  • The 2 of 34 locations that stay unreachable on every path: Jere's Mo Mos has no geometryAnchors at all in the source file (nothing to link to), and Food Court Entrance is the separate door-anchor defect.
  • The editor round-trip relocating 2 links onto the wrong polygon — that is a bridge.ts pairing bug, unrelated to importing.

issues.display_title: Issue #796: Imported doors never carry infoId, so a location anchored to a kind-less LineString stays unlinked
issues.main_description_html:
Split out of #733 (checkbox 1). Narrower sibling of #795 — that one is the whole-import failure, this is one location that stays unlinked even on the path that works.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

On the issue's asset (mall-demo-consumer.zip), 33 locations carry geometryAnchors but only 32 ever get linked:

anchored locations: 33 -> distinct linked: 32
anchored but NOT linked: Food Court Entrance (2 anchors)

Food Court Entrance (loc_60ac535cfbf635f0) is anchored to g_1bb235bf80bdf0b6 and g_0cfa9098ce884a36 — both LineStrings with no entry in kinds/. The kind fallback at src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:379-385 maps a kind-less Polygon to a room and a kind-less Point-with-anchor to a poi, but leaves a kind-less LineString undefined, so both fall through to the connections door loop and import as doors.

That door loop (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:507-530) builds {x1, y1, x2, y2, swingType, name} and never reads anchorMap — even though anchorMap is already in scope at convert.ts:349. The floor imports 36 doors, none carrying a link.

Why it is worth fixing rather than accepting

FloorplanSegment already has the field (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:96 — infoId?: string), and the manual editor UI already supports linking Information to a door (src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:549,552-554,562). So the data model and the UI both support it; only the importer skips it. An entrance with opening hours and a photo is exactly the kind of thing a mall export wants to carry.

Suggested shape

  1. In the door loop, look the geometry id up in anchorMap and copy infoId (and the anchored name, if the door has none) onto the segment. One lookup, same pattern as the area/shape branches above it.
  2. Test in src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/convert.test.ts: a fixture with a location anchored to a kind-less LineString → the produced door carries infoId, and anchored locations === distinct linked.
  3. While in there, decide whether a kind-less LineString should keep falling through to a door at all, or whether that fallback deserves to be explicit at convert.ts:379-385.

issues.display_title: Issue #797: Imported Mappedin media never renders: cdn.mappedin.com is missing from the img-src CSP
issues.main_description_html:
Split out of #733 (checkbox 2: "Imported media assets such as logos, photos, and panoramas are not automatically saved").

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The claim is worded wrong, and the difference decides the fix

The URLs are saved. Running the real round-trip (setState → buildPersistedState → JSON → hydratePersistedState) over the issue's asset:

PERSISTED photos: 27  logos: 29
AFTER hydrate(editor): records: 34  photos: 27  logos: 29   (URLs byte-identical)

convertLocations (src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:193-194) carries images[].url → Information.photos and details.icon → Information.logo, and buildPersistedState (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:85) ships them to the server with everything else.

What the user actually sees is that nothing renders — and that is our own CSP, not a missing save:

$ curl -sSI http://localhost:6060/editor   # and /v/test — identical img-src
img-src 'self' data: blob: https://*.maplibre.org https://*.openfreemap.org
        https://*.openstreetmap.org https://*.gothru.co https://img.gothru.org
        https://server.arcgisonline.com

No cdn.mappedin.com, and every render site is a plain <img src> (MediaTab.tsx:47, LabelTab.tsx:71, PreviewInfoCard.tsx:120,174, MapObjectMarkers.tsx:611, plus new Image() in floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:27) — all governed by img-src.

Decision taken: allowlist, not mirror

Per the author's call, add https://cdn.mappedin.com to the img-src directive (next.config.ts:60) and stop there. Mirroring the bytes into our own storage was considered and rejected for now:

  • the ZIP contains no image bytes at all (17 entries, every one JSON/GeoJSON), so a mirror means fetching from Mappedin's CDN at import time
  • one photo is content-length: 2371661 — a single image is larger than the whole export; ~47 unique assets per venue is roughly 100 MB of import-time traffic, needing progress UI and failure handling
  • /api/upload caps at 10 MB per file (src/app/api/upload/route.ts:6)

Known ceiling of the allowlist: the assets stay hotlinked, so they break if Mappedin revokes them or the venue is unpublished there. Revisit with a mirror if a customer hits that.

Suggested shape

  1. One entry added to img-src in next.config.ts:60. Images only — do not widen connect-src, script-src, or anything else for this.
  2. Add the case to the CSP test if one exists; otherwise assert the header contains the host, so a future CSP edit cannot silently drop it.

Second, separate defect this uncovers

Even with the CSP open, an imported logo never renders on the map or the 2D canvas:

  • resolveLabelRender (src/lib/map/objectLabel.ts:112-122) switches on info.labelType ?? "text" and only returns {mode:"logo"} under case "logo" — convertLocations never sets labelType, so every imported record falls to the text branch
  • the automatic path, closedRoomLogos, needs a.type === "closed" (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/closedRoom.ts:300-311), but the importer can only emit wall, open-to-below and hallway (convert.ts:336-340)

So after this task, an imported logo is visible only inside the Information modal previews and the detail card. Whether the importer should set labelType: "logo" when a location has an icon is a product call — raise it as its own task if wanted.

Data-quality note for whoever picks this up

20 of the 29 details.icon values are the same URL as that location's images[0] — Mappedin repeats the first photo as the icon. So the "logo" is usually a full-size ~2.3 MB photograph, not a logo. Any future mirror must de-duplicate on URL or it uploads the same JPEG twice per location.

Not a defect: panoramas

The panorama third of the original checkbox does not reproduce and needs no task. The bundle contains no panorama data of any kind — every keyword hit was a false positive (the substring 360 inside hex ids such as n_11d3d0c360486295), annotation-symbols.json is {}, and nodes/*.geojson carries only a pathfinding graph (id, geometryIds, neighbors). Panoramas enter a project solely through the TourMkr Add Panorama tool; there is no file/zip panorama import path anywhere in the app.

issues.display_title: Issue #798: Editor round-trip moves an area's Information link onto a different polygon (detected areas re-pair positionally)
issues.main_description_html:
Found while investigating #733, but this is not an import bug — it fires on any project whose walls enclose rooms, whatever created them. Filed separately for that reason.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

One editor round-trip (levelToModel → modelToLevel, i.e. opening a level and making a single edit) moves an area's Information link onto a different polygon, deletes an area, and renames most of the rest. Measured on a real imported level, 44 areas (26 manual + 18 wall-detected):

areas that LOST their infoId: 0
areas whose CENTROID moved >1px after round-trip: 17   of which carried infoId: 2
  g_efce03cb7ee1d2e1  "Washroom" -> "Room 1"  moved 1946px  info=loc_0192df0b760473f9
  g_22014d7b479080c1  "Washroom" -> "Room 7"  moved 1877px  info=loc_0192df0b760473f9

BEFORE areas: 44   AFTER areas: 43
ids present before but GONE after: g_e1a9cf5c92e09ae9 "Room 18"
areas RENAMED after round-trip: 17

No link is lost, which is why this never showed up as a missing-Information bug — the link survives and points at a room somewhere else entirely. A second round-trip returns to 44 areas and moves the same two areas again: it oscillates rather than converging, so the damage is not a one-time settle.

Mechanism

Two behaviours that are each fine alone and unsafe together.

1. Detected areas are re-paired positionally. modelToLevel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:288-291):

let id = prevDetectedAreas[i]?.id ?? nanoid();

i indexes the newly detected rooms; prevDetectedAreas[i] is the i-th previous one. detectRooms sorts area-descending, so any geometry edit that changes a room's area reorders the list and the k-th new room inherits the k-th old room's identity. levelToModel pairs the same way on the way in (bridge.ts:159-176), and its comment says so deliberately — keying off which room contains the area was tried and is worse (a walled island resolves to its parent and overwrites it).

2. The previous area is spread whole. bridge.ts:292-294:

const pa = prevAreaById.get(id);
return { ...pa, id, name: room.name, ... boundaries: room.poly.map(...) }

That spread came in 6cad4a1 ("fix: preserve vertical area links", 2026-06-23) to stop store-only fields being silently dropped — the right fix for that problem. But it means a detected area now carries infoId and every other store-only field, so a positional mismatch no longer just renames a room: it transplants the Information link onto unrelated geometry.

Manual areas are unaffected — bridge.ts:256 does prevAreaById.get(m.id), keyed by the real id. All 23 manual links, 8 shape links and 1 point link were stable across the same round-trip.

Why it matters beyond #733

An imported venue makes it easy to see (18 detected areas, 2 carrying links), but any user who draws walls that enclose rooms and links Information to one of them is exposed. The visitor-facing symptom is the worst kind: the info card opens on the wrong shop, and nothing looks broken.

Approach — decided

Narrow the spread. Keep the positional pairing exactly as it is; stop trusting its result for the fields whose stakes are high.

Rejected: giving detected rooms a stable identity instead of the array index.

  • A polygon hash breaks precisely when it is needed — a room's polygon changes on every legitimate wall edit, so every edit would drop the link.
  • The surviving variant, nearest-centroid matching, is the same heuristic as the one below, only applied somewhere with a much larger blast radius: detected-area ids are load-bearing for prevAreaById, selection state, areaMeta keys and collab. The id-collision guard at bridge.ts:285-287 exists because ids have already been stolen once.
  • The comment at bridge.ts:154-158 records that positional pairing is deliberate and that the obvious alternative (resolving by which room contains the area) was tried and is worse — a walled island resolves to its parent and overwrites it. This approach does not relitigate that.

Failure direction is the deciding argument. Narrowing the spread fails as link dropped. A stable-identity scheme that mismatches still fails as link misplaced. A dropped link is visible and the user can re-link it; a misplaced link is invisible and wrong — the info card opens on the wrong tenant and nothing looks broken. That is exactly why this bug went unnoticed: areas that LOST their infoId: 0.

Shape

Gate ...pa itself, not infoId alone — pa is the source of every store-only field, so one gate covers them all and keeps covering whatever field the next PRD adds:

id  = prevDetectedAreas[i]?.id ?? nanoid()      // unchanged
pa  = prevAreaById.get(id)
spread ...pa ONLY when the pairing is corroborated; otherwise omit it

The corroboration predicate needs a knob, and it must not be absolute pixels — scale it to the room: the new centroid still falls inside the previous ring and the two areas differ by less than N%. The area term is what closes the parent/island trap, since an island's centroid does sit inside its parent.

Test

src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/ — after a round-trip, an area carrying infoId still encloses its original centroid. Prove it load-bearing by reverting the gate: it must go red with the two "Washroom" areas named above.

Explicitly NOT fixed by this

The oscillation (44 → 43 → 44) and the 17 renames per round-trip. Same positional pairing, different surface. If those need fixing too, a stable identity becomes worth its risk — but as a separate task, after the bleeding has stopped. Do not bundle them.

Related

  • #733 / #795 / #796 — the Mappedin import work this surfaced under
  • 6cad4a1 — the spread that made positional pairing unsafe
  • 6badb0d (#735) — added the id-collision guard just above, for a neighbouring symptom of the same pairing
